title: What If Data Centers Used as Much Power as All of Japan?

scenes.text: What if the internet needed as much electricity as an entire country? It is heading there.
In 2024, the world's data centers used about 415 terawatt-hours, roughly 1.5 percent of all electricity.
The International Energy Agency expects that to reach about 945 terawatt-hours by 2030.
That is more than double in six years, and about what Japan uses in a whole year.
Artificial intelligence is the biggest driver. AI servers were already 15 percent of data center energy in 2024.
So the next time a chatbot answers in seconds, a power plant somewhere is working harder.
